page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg9i.3xlarge is a compute-focused instance within the High Clock Speed family, designed for workloads requiring strong per-core performance. It runs on the KVM hypervisor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. Compute capacity is supplied by 12 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at 3.4 GHz. System memory totals 48 GiB, establishing a ratio of 4 GiB per vCPU that balances processing power with sufficient working memory for multi-threaded applications.

The instance profile does not include bundled local disk storage, meaning persistent storage must be provisioned via remote block storage volumes. Accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs present on the system. Networking throughput is configured with a 10 Gbps baseline, ensuring steady data transit across cloud infrastructure. Standard allocations include zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires administrators to attach elastic IP resources for external routing.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, ecs.hfg9i.3xlarge optimizes expenditures by offering high per-core clock speed alongside a standard memory footprint, avoiding the costs tied to dedicated local flash media or specialized acceleration hardware. This architecture makes the server suitable for batch processing pipelines, gaming backends, mid-sized relational databases, application servers, and CI/CD build environments where high clock cycles drive direct performance gains.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg9i.3xlarge is a high clock speed virtual instance built on the KVM hypervisor within the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor running at a base clock of 3.4 GHz, the server delivers 12 dedicated vCPUs matched with 48 GiB of system memory, yielding a 4 GiB per vCPU distribution. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating network-attached block storage for persistent workloads, and contains no hardware GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is defined by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth profile, with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses allocated by default. Because of its elevated clock frequency paired with a balanced memory ratio, the instance provides cost efficiency for throughput-dependent applications without the overhead of underutilized specialized accelerators. Appropriate workloads include latency-sensitive business applications, compilation pipelines, web application tiers, and relational database management systems requiring consistent dedicated CPU execution.
